stance_basis: directly quoted concluding that consumption of bass from Lake Jocassee is inadvisable due to mercury levels
summary: Abernathy (1975) is a researcher whose study found dangerously high mercury levels in Lake Jocassee fish, particularly largemouth bass, exceeding the FDA maximum methylmercury limit of 0.5 ug/g. Abernathy concluded that consumption of bass from Lake Jocassee is inadvisable, noting that even small daily quantities of fish would exceed the allowable daily intake of mercury. The study also reported elevated mercury levels in fish from downstream Lakes Keowee and Hartwell.
complaint_summary: Abernathy (1975) concludes that consumption of bass from Lake Jocassee is inadvisable because all fish samples exceeded the FDA maximum mercury level and even small daily quantities of fish would exceed the allowable daily intake of 30 ug of mercury per day.
